newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George says 1st qtr satisfactory.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George says 1st qtr satisfactory.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Wednesday trading for it and its recently-acquired Advance Bank Australia Ltd in the three months to end-December had been satisfactory.
However, St George managing director Jim Sweeney told the company's annual meeting that the bank would continue to experience further pressure on margins during 1997.
"It is gratifying to say that trading in the first quarter has been satisfactory in both St George and Advance," chairman Frank Conroy told the annual meeting.
"The directors are also pleased with the gain of new housing loans, given so much competition in this area," he said.
Conroy said that in considering future performance, the bank would have to await the outcome of the current Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial sector.

Sweeney said the demand for housing is expected to grow as the impact of recent cuts in interest rates begins to stimulate the market with volume growth offsetting some of the impact of reduced spreads.
"Nonetheless we continue to expect margin pressure to be a feature of our operating environment in 1997," Sweeney told the meeting.
St George in November announced a 17.7 percent rise in net profit to A$159.51 million for the year to September 30, 1996.
Advance Bank Australia Ltd, which is now wholly-owned by St George, last month reported a 12.48 percent rise in net profit after abnormals to A$90.10 million in the six months to November 30, 1996.
Conroy said a decision on a further capital raising for the bank would be made before mid-year.
"The directors are yet to determine the final mix of capital instruments and whether there will be any right to participation for existing ordinary shareholders," he told the meeting.
"There are several options available to directors. A decision will be made on this before mid-year," he said.
